hens_rule_text: Up to 10 hens allowed on a home lot; one secondary source ties this to a minimum lot size of about 10,000 sq ft. No roosters.
permit_notes: No general chicken permit was confirmed for the city; a secondary source suggested permits may apply in certain zoning districts, but this was not verified in the code text found.
setback_notes: No specific setback distance in feet was found in available extracts of Sec. 6-228; the code instead requires sanitary housing meeting Cumberland County Board of Health standards.
coop_rules: Coops must be kept clean and ventilated, placed in the backyard, with proper manure disposal, and must meet Cumberland County Board of Health sanitary standards.
zoning_notes: Keeping animals that are a nuisance or hazard, including by crowing, is separately prohibited, which is the likely basis for the rooster ban alongside the fowl-specific rule.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: BackyardChickens.com, Fayetteville North Carolina Chicken Ordinance
Chicken.io, Fayetteville North Carolina Chicken Ordinance

research_notes: The exact city code (Sec. 6-228) was not located on Municode or an archived copy; all figures (10 hens, no roosters, Cumberland County Board of Health sanitary standard, possible 10,000 sq ft minimum lot) come from consistent secondary chicken-law sites quoting the section number, not from the primary text itself. Setback distance and permit rules in specific zoning districts remain unconfirmed.
